about: Release channels the weekly harness-convention monitor watches, one entry per harness folder under src/apothem/harnesses/. scripts/dev/check_vendor_releases.py compares each channel's current version, or an installer address's redirect target, with the one last reviewed, and scripts/README.md describes every field. After you re-check a pin against a new release or target, update that channel's reviewed, reviewed_on and reviewed_from. A trigger on a version channel keeps failing the check until you remove or change it. A trigger on an installer address stops once reviewed records the new target, so record that target only after the trigger's action is done.

channels.name: opencode-ai
channels.evidence: the `opencode-ai` npm package still install OpenCode 1

trigger.action: Read what opencode-ai's latest tag names now: this trigger fires on a release past major 1, and when the package or that tag is gone. If it names an OpenCode 2 release, this is the second switch signal in the OpenCode decision of 2026-11-03: move the OpenCode install to version-aware output, writing OpenCode 2's own formats where OpenCode 2 runs. Remove or change this trigger once that is done; until then it fails the check every week.

channels.note: OpenCode 1, the default line. With no version given, opencode.ai/install installs this tag's version when it is a 1.x release, else the newest v1 release on GitHub, and it refuses a requested version of 2 or later. So this tag moving to 2.x does not change what that installer installs; the opencode.ai/install channel below watches where the installer itself redirects.

channels.name: anomalyco/opencode
channels.note: The repository publishes the releases of both lines, so a new major line shows here whatever npm package it ships as: OpenCode 2 first appeared here as v2.2.0 on 2026-10-27, while its npm package is @opencode/cli, not opencode-ai. Only stable releases tagged v followed by the version count, which skips the repository's process-daemon and pull-request releases. The pin read the v2.2.5 source on 2026-11-03.

channels.name: opencode.ai/install

trigger.action: opencode.ai/install no longer redirects to the OpenCode 1 installer script. Read the script it serves now. If it still installs OpenCode 1, record the new target in the pin and in this channel's reviewed field. If it installs OpenCode 2, this is the second switch signal in the OpenCode decision of 2026-11-03: move the OpenCode install to version-aware output, writing OpenCode 2's own formats where OpenCode 2 runs. Recording the new target in reviewed stops this trigger, so record it only once the switch is done, then remove or change this trigger.

channels.note: The default installer, which the OpenCode decision names as a switch signal. On 2026-11-03 it answered 307, redirecting to the install script on the v1 branch, which says it installs only OpenCode 1 and points OpenCode 2 users to opencode.ai/v2/install. A change inside the v1 script does not change the redirect, so this channel does not see it.
